name: System-protection facilities
desc: Require hybrids to install protection that blocks injections or withdrawals beyond their granted rights.

letters.desc: AEMA proposes a secure, standardized operator-facility interface with automated dispatch and auditable telemetry as the modern system protection mechanism, mirroring demand-response verification practices while preserving cybersecurity and operational autonomy.
quotes: Under this model, the operator issues a dispatch signal, for example a 100-megawatt curtailment request to the facility's registered energy management interface. The facility's flexibility management platform executes the reduction automatically and provides real-time or near-real-time, auditable telemetry back to the operator to confirm compliance.

letters.desc: AEMA argues that a load with a tariff-backed operational limit monitored in real time by the grid operator delivers a reliability service equivalent to generation, and therefore deserves equivalent treatment in the interconnection process.
quotes: When a large load commits to a tariff-backed operational limit—monitored in real-time by the grid operator—it provides a reliability service physically equivalent to generation.

letters.desc: The filer supports requiring any existing generator entering partial suspension to serve a new large load to undergo an SSR/RMR-type study that covers both reliability and resource adequacy. It notes FERC can impose this requirement regardless of whether it extends its jurisdictional reach over load interconnection.
quotes: United agrees that such facilities should go through an SSR/RMR type study, and that such studies should include evaluation of potential resource adequacy concerns. United also emphasizes that the Commission can take this action regardless of whether it asserts jurisdiction over the interconnection of new large loads directly to the transmission system.

letters.desc: AES strongly supports customer protection requirements: network upgrade costs should fall on the large load, termination fees must compensate the utility for stranded infrastructure, and co-location incentives must not shift costs onto existing ratepayers.
quotes: There is a clear role for the Commission in ensuring that certain cost-recovery mechanisms are just and reasonable (such as cost recovery related to the construction of network upgrades if a large load abandons the interconnection prior to taking retail service).
these incentives should not unduly harm other customers on the system, whether through cost-shifting, or otherwise.

letters.desc: ATC supports strict system protection facilities that can disconnect non-conforming loads and enforce injection and withdrawal limits. ATC backs NERC standards for large loads with oscillatory behavior and supports penalties for unauthorized injections or withdrawals, paired with transparency requirements.
quotes: strict operational limitations must be enforced, as unauthorized injections or withdrawals, particularly with oscillating data center loads, cannot be tolerated.

ATC strongly supports principles that uphold cost responsibility and maintain reliability, including proposed penalties for unauthorized injections or withdrawals.  However, any implementation plan must avoid unintended cost shifts and ensure transparency for transmission customers.

ATC strongly supports the implementation of robust operational standards for large load interconnections, particularly those exhibiting significant oscillatory behavior, because such behavior can cause voltage and frequency instability if not properly managed.

letters.desc: ATC calls for mandatory system protection facilities in any co-study scenario, warning that the inability to curtail firm service means full reliability impacts must be analyzed to prevent catastrophic consequences.
quotes: to the extent hybrid facilities are studied together, safeguards such as process matching and system protection facilities must be incorporated.
Misalignment between load and generation at a shared interconnection point can lead to unintended injections or withdrawals from the transmission system.
transmission owners lack the necessary tools to curtail firm service; therefore, the full impacts of any hybrid facility must be considered to prevent catastrophic consequences.

letters.desc: APS supports safeguards against cost-shifting to existing customers and emphasizes that large load customers must pay for their own infrastructure investments.
quotes: Will there be safeguards to ensure that there is no cost shift between new large load customers and other transmission or retail customer classes?
substantial infrastructure investments required to connect and serve these large loads will be paid for by those new large load customers, not existing customers.

letters.desc: CAISO calls protection facility requirements the most critical reform principle. It recommends requiring large loads to submit steady-state, RMS, and EMT behavioral models and to provide real-time component-level telemetry, mirroring standards applied to large generators and inverter-based resources.
quotes: The CAISO believes this principle is among the most critical to establish.  As NERC has already demonstrated, large loads can affect frequency, voltage, and power quality just as large generators do.
The CAISO also recommends that any reform include the requirement that large loads provide load profiles and expected behavior models as part of the interconnection process.

large loads should be required to submit detailed steady-state, dynamic (RMS), and, for certain facilities, electromagnetic transient (EMT) models reflecting expected demand behavior, similar to the modeling requirements currently applied to inverter-based generators.
The CAISO recommends that any final rule require large loads and hybrid facilities to provide transmission providers with real-time telemetry at the component level.

letters.org: CHAMBER OF COMMERCE OF THE UNITED STATES
letters.desc: The Chamber stresses that large loads must not compromise reliability or impose adverse impacts on existing customers, and that cost allocation should ensure interconnections lower rather than raise rates for everyone else.
quotes: Grid Reliability and Resilience: The integration of large loads must not compromise grid reliability or resilience. The Commission should ensure the grid can accommodate these loads without adverse impacts on existing customers or the overall integrity of the grid.

large loads are committed to paying their full cost of service for the energy and infrastructure supporting the electric service they require. Ultimately, large load interconnections should result in lower, rather than elevated, electricity rates for all other customers. The Commission's efforts to streamline large load interconnections should ensure that costs are allocated commensurate with the benefits received from any needed network upgrades.

letters.desc: Crusoe supports mandatory system protection facilities for hybrid interconnections to prevent injections or withdrawals that exceed contracted rights, with minimum telemetry and operating standards.
quotes: The Commission should require hybrid interconnections to install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights available to the interconnection customer.

letters.desc: DCC calls for explicit grandfathering and legally enforceable transition provisions in the final rule so that projects with existing commitments under current rules are not disrupted by prospective reforms.
quotes: DCC's Initial Comments strongly advocated for "clear and legally enforceable transition provisions" to ensure that reforms aimed at improving future processes do not disrupt projects that have made significant commitments under existing rules.
The Commission should incorporate explicit grandfathering and transition pathways in any final rule to provide this essential certainty.

letters.desc: DPN supports requiring system protection facilities on hybrid interconnections to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals beyond the granted rights.
quotes: any hybrid interconnection shall be required to install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights.

letters.desc: EDF supports requiring hybrid interconnections to install telemetry and protection facilities that enforce injection and withdrawal rights and prevent unauthorized grid use.
quotes: the Commission should require hybrid interconnections to install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights available to the interconnection customer.

letters.desc: Traditional industrial load owners have been reliably served for decades without NERC registration and should not be newly required to register. ELCON accepts limited, targeted registration for data centers where reliability risks are specific and compliance burdens are minimal, but opposes any rule that inadvertently reclassifies industrial owners as public utilities.
quotes: ELCON maintains that the electric system has reliably served industrial load for decades and it remains unnecessary to require owners/operators of traditional large industrial loads to be NERC registered entities and subjected to mandatory reliability standards.

ELCON does not oppose limited registration for data centers and other computational loads as described by NERC's Large Load Task Force in Whitepaper #1 that carry minimal compliance burdens that are commensurate with specifically identified reliability risks posed by the nature of these emerging loads.

ELCON respectfully urges FERC to ensure that these changes do not have the unintended consequence of making new registrants "public utilities" under the broad definition of that term in Section 201(e) of the FPA.

letters.desc: ENGIE agrees that hybrid applicants should install system protection facilities to prevent unauthorized flows, but insists owners must have the flexibility to choose their protection systems as long as they meet industry standards.
quotes: hybrid facility owners should have the flexibility to install protection systems of their choice as long as they meet the requisite industry standards.

letters.desc: Entergy argues that large loads should not interconnect without verifying adequate generation capacity. Resource adequacy review is a state retail-jurisdictional matter that the Commission must not displace.
quotes: Large loads should not be permitted to interconnect without consideration of available generation capacity.  For example, if existing generation is being used to serve a large load (rather than the construction of new generation), studies to ensure reliability and local resource adequacy will be needed.

letters.desc: Entergy calls on FERC to affirmatively confirm that in-progress and existing agreements are grandfathered, noting broad commenter consensus on this point. It also urges a significant transition period before any new rule takes effect, with the length tied to the final rule's scope.
quotes: the Commission should affirmatively ensure no retroactive impact on in-process or existing agreements
A significant transition period will be necessary for states, stakeholders and transmission owners to adjust to a new regulatory scheme.

letters.desc: Eolian draws on precedents including ATC's paper-mill contracts and MISO's surplus interconnection service to demonstrate that operating limits on hybrid net injections and withdrawals can be reliably enforced through protection equipment and contractual commitments.
quotes: Taken together, these examples clearly demonstrate that operating limits on hybrid facilities' net injections and withdrawals to and from the grid can be safely enforced, and therefore assigned based on the amounts requested, and not necessarily their nameplate capabilities, in such cases where such requested injections and withdrawals are below the amount of nameplate generation and load respectively.

letters.desc: Fervo supports tailored protection requirements that account for geothermal's stable operating profile and minimal system risk, rather than broadly prescriptive mandates that do not reflect geothermal's actual operational characteristics.
quotes: Fervo agrees that appropriate system-protection requirements may be necessary for hybrid facilities but emphasizes that such requirements should be proportionate to the actual operational characteristics and risks of the resource. Geothermal has stable and predictable operating profiles and does not exhibit fast-changing injection or withdrawal patterns that drive many protection concerns for other technologies.
protection systems for these hybrids can be tailored rather than broadly prescriptive, ensuring reliability without imposing unnecessary or overly burdensome technical mandates

Fervo encourages the Commission to ensure that any enforcement mechanisms or operational limits for unauthorized injections or withdrawals reflect the physical realities of hybrid geothermal operations and do not inadvertently constrain resources that already pose minimal system-protection risk.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy supports protecting existing retail customers from cost shifts driven by large load interconnections, but argues this can be achieved through rolled-in rates combined with state tariff and agreement mechanisms rather than direct assignment.
quotes: Rather than risk extended delay due to jurisdictional challenges and other cost allocation battles, the Commission should employ its long-standing rolled-in rate approach for network upgrades in conjunction with facilitating customer protections to ensure that other retail load customers are not adversely affected by large load interconnections.

letters.desc: A central aim of the proposal is shielding existing residential, small business, and industrial customers from the cost of upgrades built for hyperscale loads. Developer collateral, a minimum-demand floor, and direct cost causation all serve to keep that infrastructure off the bills of customers who do not benefit from it.
quotes: To protect existing customers from residual exposure, the data center developer would also maintain creditworthy collateral support equal to the remaining unrecovered balance of the expansion facilities over the life of the agreement.

the customer's transmission-rate contribution could be calculated based on the higher of actual demand or a minimum contractual-demand threshold, preventing cost-shifting through underutilization. Likewise, expansion-rate obligations could be reallocated annually as additional customers interconnect to the same facilities, reducing the cost burden borne by any individual participant over time.
Households and small businesses would no longer be required to subsidize infrastructure developed primarily to serve hyperscale facilities.

letters.desc: Google supports uniform safeguards that apply to all new large loads above a MW threshold, regardless of end-use sector, to protect existing customers from cost shifting and ensure new loads pay their full cost of service.
quotes: All new loads interconnecting to the transmission system—whether paired with co-located or electrically proximate generation or not—should be subject to safeguards to protect other customers and ratepayers.
The Commission's reforms should apply uniformly to all new large loads (above a certain MW-level threshold) that seek to interconnect to the transmission system, regardless of end-use sector.

letters.desc: GridStor asks that new large-load rules not inadvertently disadvantage ESRs, calling it imperative that ESRs be considered separately and that large-load queuing requirements not be imposed on resources already in generator queues.
quotes: To the extent that the Commission seeks to put new requirements on large loads, it is imperative that ESRs be considered distinctly and separately from large loads.

For example, it would be inappropriate and onerously duplicative to apply large loads queuing requirements as discussed in the ANOPR to apply to ESRs. Today, ESRs already participate in generator interconnection queuing processes with required deposits and readiness requirements, and ESRs execute interconnection agreements in a well-understood manner.

letters.desc: The filing warns that large loads contracting existing generation will siphon power from the grid, leaving residential and commercial customers vulnerable to scarcity pricing and blackouts. It calls for a framework that protects current customers from the distortions caused by loads the size of small cities.
quotes: new large load contracts with generators who currently serve the aggregate load of electricity customers throughout the country, from residential customers to major industrial load, will siphon power from the grid and leave customers who rely on the bulk power system vulnerable to scarcity pricing and possible shortages and blackouts.

letters.desc: The commenter opposes leaving protection device installation and operation solely with the load facility because a malicious actor could bypass them. Grid operators should install, maintain, and operate these devices. Penalties for unauthorized injections or withdrawals and mandatory curtailment authority are also recommended.
quotes: I have significant concern that allotting the installation and operation of protection devices to the load facility would not protect against malicious actors since they could simply bypass these protections on their facility. I would recommend at least the local grid operator, install, maintain, and operate the protection.
a hybrid interconnection customer should be subject to penalties for unauthorized injections or withdrawals (outside of a certain reasonable minimum threshold).

Recommend the possibility that curtailment may be mandatory at the system operator's instruction (for emergency situations) and request clarity on how curtailment priority will be established relative to other resources.

letters.desc: If DER resources are to receive any interconnection credit, the filer argues they must meet the same contractual firmness, metering, and verification standards as generation interconnections, including binding financial penalties for non-performance.
quotes: such contributions must be demonstrated through the same rigorous interconnection study methodology applied to all other resources: Locational specificity... Temporal certainty... Operational firmness... Verification and measurement

letters.desc: IECA supports system protection facilities and highlights open questions about what happens to grid reliability during full or partial outages of either the Data Center or generator. It defers to NERC on bulk electric system reliability standards and threshold sizing.
quotes: some provision should be made for what will happen when the resource (i.e., generator) or the load (i.e., the Data Center) experiences a full or partial outage, whether scheduled or unscheduled.

we support requirements to install system protection facilities to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals, but we also recognize and support the ability of Data Centers relying on the grid as a backstop source of electric energy when a co-located generator experiences a full or partial outage.

Reliability and resource adequacy issues are affected much more by loads of 100 MW or larger, so setting an artificially low threshold could be problematic for purposes of addressing grid reliability.

letters.desc: IECA asks FERC to define a range of acceptable transmission system protections for each of three co-location configurations (firm, generator-contingent, and interruptible) and to make those protections flexible enough for both high-redundancy and lower-redundancy data centers.
quotes: any guidance, policies, rules, or other regulations issued by the Commission in response to the Secretary's ANOPR will need to be flexible enough to encourage and accommodate both types of Data Centers.

the Commission and its Staff should now have a relatively complete record on "co-location" issues in PJM on which to formulate and propose guidance in response to the ANOPR regarding the range of acceptable transmission system protection provisions that counterparties could apply to co-location arrangements involving large loads and co-located generation resources located at the same point of interconnection or at "proximate" points of interconnection with the interstate transmission grid.

letters.desc: ISO-NE urges that protection schemes be simple, standardized, and limited to conditions at the point of interconnection. Complex schemes would create unmanageable operational risk for system operators.
quotes: ISO-NE believes that protection schemes must be simple, straightforward, and standardized.  In addition, protection schemes should only act behind a Point of Interconnection for conditions at the Point of Interconnection.  Using more complex schemes would be unmanageable for operators, adding operational complexity risks.

letters.desc: The filing frames its customer-protective mechanisms as the way to ensure large load growth does not shift costs onto other customers. It catalogs dedicated substations, upfront funding, and other provisions as in active use to protect all customers.
quotes: its member utilities have long employed public power tariffs, special contracts, and bilateral service agreements to integrate large loads while protecting all customers from undue cost-
a summary of the tariff and contractual frameworks those utilities are using to ensure large load customers pay their fair share

LPPC member utilities are employing a variety of customer-protective mechanisms, including dedicated substations, upfront infrastructure funding requirements, take-or-pay provisions, minimum billing demand charges, exit fees, and bring-your-own-power arrangements, to ensure large load growth does not burden existing ratepayers.

letters.desc: LS Power calls for rules that prevent curtailment of flexible large loads from suppressing competitive energy market price signals and from distorting resource adequacy planning. Open-access principles prohibit discriminatory treatment of new large load relative to existing load or generation.
quotes: it is also critical that the relevant regional energy markets send the appropriate price signal to indicate scarcity of supply resources such that the curtailment of flexible large loads cannot be used to undermine competitive energy market pricing by failing to reflect curtailable load in resource adequacy planning.
To introduce resource adequacy as a consideration in determining whether and at what cost to interconnect new large load would necessarily discriminate against that new load and existing generators.

letters.desc: Meta supports installation of system protection facilities to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals exceeding respective interconnection rights for hybrid facilities.
quotes: Meta agrees that interconnection of hybrid facilities should require installation of 'the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed [those] respective rights'

letters.desc: The Michigan AG joins a multi-state coalition urging FERC to make ratepayer protection a central priority throughout this rulemaking, not an afterthought.
quotes: The Attorney General also replies to express support for the request raised in comment by a group of several states' attorneys general and ratepayer advocates for FERC to "meaningfully prioritize ratepayer protections during this rulemaking process."

letters.org: National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners
letters.desc: NARUC says any rule must ensure large load interconnections comply with NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions, including system protection requirements and penalties for unauthorized power injections or withdrawals.
quotes: Any rule must also ensure that all large load interconnections comply with NERC reliability standards and Open Access Transmission Tariff provisions, including technical requirements for system protection facilities for hybrid projects and potential penalties for unauthorized power injections or withdrawals.

letters.org: National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners
letters.desc: NARUC emphasizes shielding residential, commercial, and manufacturing customers from improper cost shifts and discriminatory procedures. It points to state tariff protections such as collateral, demand charges, and stranded-cost safeguards as evidence states already protect non-large-load customers.
quotes: The abundance of recent state undertakings demonstrate that state commissions are in the best position to ensure rational and efficient interconnections of new large loads while protecting all customers (including residential, commercial and large manufacturing customers) from improper cost-shifts or unfair interconnection processes.

If FERC issues different federal rules for interconnection of data center loads, this may lead to increased costs or discriminatory procedures for other important end-use customers, such as Virginia manufacturers developing critical components

it remains unclear how cost allocation would work if some large loads have already paid for network upgrades through a federal interconnection process, making them exempt from other transmission costs at the retail level.  This could lead to costs being shifted to other retail ratepayers, while limiting the states’ ability to appropriately allocate costs and protect other customers.

this new large load tariff requires a minimum contract term of 14 years, a maximum ramp period of four years, minimum collateral requirements, and minimum demand charges based on contracted capacity.  All these protections will ensure that costs are not shifted to non-large load customers.
These terms ensure large loads pay their share even if they use less power than planned and prevent potential stranded asset costs from being passed to other retail ratepayers.

letters.desc: NRECA supports requiring system protection facilities at hybrid interconnections but notes they address only extreme events and can fail. Full reliability studies remain necessary alongside physical protection equipment.
quotes: hybrid interconnections should be required to install system protection and control facilities to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights (e.g., leaning on the transmission system when co-located generation is not adequate to meet the large load's need).

letters.org: Natural Resource Defense CouncilSustainable FERC ProjectClean Air Task Force ,Coalition for Affordable Utility Services and Energy Efficie ,EARTHJUSTICE ,ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENSE FUND ,MONTANA ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION CENTER ,Sierra Club ,Southern Environmental Law Center ,
letters.desc: Any interconnection rule must protect existing ratepayers from cost shifts, reliability risk, and unfair curtailment allocation. Control technologies and clear wholesale curtailment guidelines are the primary mechanisms the filers endorse.
quotes: Control technologies are a better approach because they can allow direct control of injections or withdrawals and thus prevent any harm associated with unauthorized actions, such as distortions in market prices or threats to reliability.
FERC must establish guidelines to limit unfair allocation of reliability risks at the wholesale level.

letters.org: New York State Reliability Council, L.L.C.
letters.desc: Large loads must be evaluated for their interaction with automatic underfrequency load shedding (UFLS) programs, which are the last-line defense against system collapse. UFLS functionality must be assured through proactive design before interconnection, not reactive review after the fact.
quotes: Large loads – whether co-located with generating facilities or standalone – will most likely be interconnected at voltage levels exceeding the 100kV North American Electric Reliability Corporation ("NERC") definition of Bulk Electric System. As a result, this will bring the interconnection of such large load facilities within the scope of the Commission-approved Electric Reliability Organization ("ERO") mandatory requirements that are designed to preserve the reliable operation of the power system.

While there are many areas of reliability related concern, one that has not been raised but is vital is automatic UFLS programs and their role as the last line of defense used during periods of stressed system conditions after operators have exhausted all of their manual load shedding (i.e., rotating blackout) options.
Potential adverse impacts to reliability and resilience must be examined in advance (not reactively) and be addressed through the design of the interconnection facility.

The NYSRC is in support of the Commission's inquiry into necessary reforms to effectuate the interconnection of large loads. Accordingly, the NYSRC submits that automatic UFLS programs must be considered in the design of large load facilities interconnecting to the transmission system from a preemptive or proactive planning perspective.

letters.org: New York Transmission OwnersCentral Hudson Gas & Electric CorporationNew York Power Authority ,New York State Electric & Gas Corp. and Rochester Gas and El ,Niagara Mohawk d/b/a/ National Grid ,Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc. and Orange and ,Long Island Power Authority ,
letters.desc: The NYTOs support assigning NERC reliability obligations to the entity that owns or operates BES-connected equipment, whether a transmission owner or the large-load customer itself. They oppose shifting NERC accountability to transmission owners for equipment owned by third-party load customers, warning that this would blur enforcement lines and introduce operational risk.
quotes: Large-load customers taking retail delivery service at transmission-level voltages should be subject to enforceable reliability obligations, including compliance with applicable NERC standards.

Shifting NERC accountability from a customer constructing, owning or operating BES-connected equipment to the Transmission Owner would introduce operational risk and blur enforcement lines by making Transmission Owners responsible for the actions of third parties like large load customers.

letters.org: North Carolina Utilities Commission Public Staff
letters.desc: The Public Staff warns the rules could create a new customer class with unduly preferential treatment and asks that any rule place no constraints on state authority over retail rates, generation, and siting. It supports preserving states' ability to use large-load tariffs and flexibility requirements.
quotes: the proposed rules risk creating a new class of customer that would receive unduly preferential treatment.

any final rule should place no constraints, express or implied, on the authority of states to set the terms and rates for retail customers over generation facilities, or over the siting of transmission.
limit[ing] States’ ability to implement pro ability to implement protective measures, such as large load tariffs and flexibility requirements

letters.org: Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel
letters.desc: OCC supports requiring a two-part SSR/RMR analysis plus a three-year forward resource adequacy assessment when generation capacity suspends to serve new load, with replacement capacity costs borne by the interconnecting customer rather than existing consumers.
quotes: the RTO or regional planning authority should perform a forward-looking resource adequacy assessment- spanning at least three years – to determine whether the suspension would erode reserve margins or necessitate additional capacity procurement.
The cost of obtaining replacement capacity should not be borne by existing consumers who have relied on and been paying for the suspension resources for many years.

letters.desc: ODEC supports requiring large loads and hybrid facilities to meet all NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions, and calls for NERC registration of large loads. It also flags that current system protection schemes may cause cascading disconnections in complex multi-substation campuses and asks FERC or NERC to develop targeted standards.
quotes: ODEC supports requiring utilities serving large loads to meet all applicable NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions.

letters.desc: OPSI supports measures protecting retail customers from costs they did not cause, preserving state prudency review rights, and ensuring resource adequacy obligations are clearly assigned when large loads are added faster than new generation can materialize.
quotes: FERC should "preserve and affirm states' retail regulatory authority under the FPA, ensure that large load interconnections do not compromise grid reliability or impose undue costs on retail customers, and respect state tools for promoting system flexibility and equitable cost allocation."
It is imperative that large loads looking to interconnect bear their fair share of transmission costs and that the Commission deter harmful speculation as these loads seek to interconnect.

FERC rules must not impede the state's traditional right to perform prudency reviews and conduct cost causation analysis necessary to protect local ratepayers from costs they did not cause, especially where transmission charges are based on withdrawal rights.
The Commission should clarify who is responsible for meeting resource adequacy and reliability obligations in both restructured and vertically integrated contexts.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers urge FERC to require minimum contract terms, an 85% minimum demand charge, demand ramping requirements, and financial collateral from large loads so that stranded transmission costs do not fall on other ratepayers if a large load reduces load or exits.
quotes: The Joint Consumer Advocates support a package of ratepayer protections to the extent that the Commission finds them to be jurisdictional: 1) minimum contractual duration, renewal, and cancellation provisions; 2) minimum demand payments and demand ramping requirements; 3) financial collateral and guarantees.

The Joint Consumer Advocates support the establishment of clear contract terms regarding duration, renewal, and termination fees. Additionally, a minimum demand charge of 85% of forecasted peak demand at the conclusion of the ramp period would be reasonable.

letters.desc: PPL supports requiring hybrid co-located facilities to install system protection equipment that prevents unauthorized injections or withdrawals beyond their interconnection rights, citing its own experience with the Susquehanna Nuclear load arrangement and prior advocacy in related dockets.
quotes: any Commission action on co-located load should follow two 'North Star' principles: (1) Protect the safety and reliability of the bulk electric system; and (2) Prevent subsidization of new loads by network customers.

hybrid facilities 'shall be required to install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights.' Here again, the ANOPR hits the mark exactly.

letters.desc: Shell Energy asks FERC to ensure expedited large load study processes do not cause delays, cost shifts, or new uncertainty for generators already in interconnection queues, consistent with the goals of Order No. 2023.
quotes: Shell Energy does not support existing generation having discriminatory and punitive provisions that it must pay for network upgrades for engaging in a bilateral capacity sale.
Expedited study processes envisioned under this ANOPR should not cause delays, uncertainty, or allocation of new costs to generator interconnection customers already in queues.

letters.org: Southern Company Services, Inc.Alabama Power CompanyGeorgia Power Company ,Mississippi Power Company ,
letters.desc: The filing details state-approved mechanisms that shield existing customers from large-load costs, including minimum bill obligations, collateral requirements, and termination protection. It frames these as proven safeguards against subsidization.
quotes: Southern Companies are connecting large load retail customers quickly and efficiently, while protecting customers from cost-shifting, as identified in the ANOPR and the President’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge

Georgia Power Company has implemented several mechanisms aimed to protect existing customers, including minimum bill obligations for large loads, long-term contractual commitments, collateral requirements, termination protection, and regulatory review and accountability for customer-specific arrangements.

Southern Companies have integrated large volumes of new loads in a manner that not only protects existing customers from additional costs, but actually benefits these existing customers through allocating fixed-cost recovery across a broader customer base.

letters.desc: SPP warns that protection systems cannot fully guard against the fast dynamic effects of a large generator trip at a hybrid facility, including rapid frequency excursions and relay misoperations. Full-load study is required to ensure protection coordination.
quotes: system protection facilities may not fully protect the grid from stability issues, and as such, the full load at a hybrid facility should be considered when applying a MW threshold.

Even with system protections in place, very rapid withdrawals of large amounts of power can adversely affect the transmission grid (e.g., through rapid frequency excursions and unintended protection operations). All generators are susceptible to unexpected tripping, and protection schemes themselves may fail under fast dynamic conditions.

letters.desc: Talen wants existing generation protected from undue discrimination, opposing BYOG mandates and disproportionate reliability studies that disadvantage loads contracting with existing units. It argues new and existing resources should compete on equal footing to avoid accelerating premature retirements.
quotes: Proposals that require new large load customers to bring their own new generation are discriminatory.

enhanced reliability studies that apply disproportionate requirements to large loads contracting with existing generation as opposed to new generation are unlawful and will result in undue discrimination against existing generation.
the Commission should allow existing generation resources to compete on equal footing with new generation resources to serve large load customers.
policies favoring new generation at the expense of existing resources risks accelerating retirement of highly reliable, dispatchable, and baseload units.

Conditioning customer interconnections on BYOG or instructing PJM to deny service conflicts with bedrock open-access principles FERC established in Order No. 888 and Order No. 2000, which mandate non-discriminatory transmission service under a Commission-approved tariff.

Instructing PJM to pick winners and losers among loads would undermine the Commission’s open-access framework and invite litigation over undue discrimination, delaying urgently needed reliability solutions.

letters.desc: Terraflux agrees that hybrid interconnections should be required to install system protections.
quotes: We agree with the sixth principle's assertion that hybrid interconnections shall be required to install system protections.

letters.desc: Tesla recommends standardized minimum interconnection standards for large loads covering ramp rate, load stability, and voltage ride-through.
quotes: Tesla recommends establishing minimum interconnection standards for large loads, including ramp rate, load stability, and voltage ride-through rate as standardized with the process.

letters.desc: TAPS insists that system protection facilities are the fundamental safeguard for enforcing hybrid facility limits, and that operational limitations may also be necessary since protective equipment can fail. Financial penalties alone are insufficient given the potential severity of grid impacts.
quotes: it is essential that they be required to have system protection facilities/mechanisms/schemes that are adequate to enforce these limits. That is the fundamental premise for studying Qualifying Large Hybrid Facilities based on their requested injection or withdrawal rights.

letters.desc: UCS recommends that system protection facilities enforce both duration and voltage limits on inadvertent export or import events, not just capacity limits. The filing calls on FERC to convene a technical expert workgroup to set minimum requirements, and warns that rules should not rely solely on financial penalties as a substitute for engineering requirements.
quotes: A future set of proposed rules forthcoming from the Commission should be informed by technical considerations and not be limited to a financial penalty framework.

system protection facilities must: 1. Ensure that if the facility exceeds the allowed limits, its import or export is returned to the allowed limits within a fixed time period, defined by the TSO. 2. During the inadvertent export or import event, maintain the voltage at the point of interconnection within limits defined by the TSO.

we recommend that the Commission convene a workgroup of technical experts to develop such requirements. These requirements should be responsive to available technical capability and should prioritize reliability while avoiding excessive costs to developers and consumers.

letters.desc: The filers explicitly request that FERC authorize utility-administered curtailment of large loads during grid emergencies, citing near-miss incidents in high data center buildout regions.
quotes: Authorizing utility-administered curtailment protocols during grid emergencies.

letters.desc: Vantage urges that projects with existing interconnection agreements be grandfathered under current frameworks with only voluntary opt-in to new programs. Projects that already have study results in hand should not face costly restudies or additional delays.
quotes: it is imperative that projects with existing interconnection agreements are permitted to move forward under their current frameworks and grandfathered from any reform that is put in place – unless they voluntarily opt in to a new, Commission-approved tariff interconnection program that appropriately implements the guiding principles of the proposed ANOPR.
projects that are in advanced stages of development and have study results in hand should not be subjected to costly restudies and additional delays.

letters.desc: Verrus agrees with CAISO and TAPS that strict protections, including real-time telemetry and potentially physical circuit protection schemes, are needed to make asset-backed flexibility commitments credible enough for transmission providers to rely on in lieu of network upgrades.
quotes: Verrus agrees with the California Independent System Operator ("CAISO") and Transmission Access Policy Study Group ("TAPS") that "strict, unwavering protections" are necessary to ensure that flexible loads meet their curtailment obligations.

letters.desc: The VSCC argues state regulators must retain authority to balance economic development against protection of retail customers, resource adequacy, and reliability, and that FERC jurisdiction would undermine this protection.
quotes: a range of commenters expressed concern with the Commission's assertion of jurisdiction, which both deprives states of the opportunity to address large load interconnection issues (which more than half the states are already doing), while subjecting any Final Rule in this proceeding to legal challenge under the Federal Power Act.

letters.desc: Vistra identifies a clear discrimination risk: transmission owners with generation affiliates have incentives to favor loads served by those affiliates. National rules must explicitly prohibit undue discrimination and include ongoing compliance mechanisms.
quotes: Transmission owners that have unregulated generation affiliates or operate in states where large loads have the option to select a competitive supplier have a clear incentive to favor the interconnection of new large loads that agree to take electric service from their affiliated generation.  This incentive creates the potential for a textbook example of undue discrimination that must be remedied by a set of national rules that explicitly bar undue discrimination and with on-going compliance checks to ensure those rules are working as designed.

letters.desc: Vistra supports transmission providers' authority to require circuit breakers, telemetry, and other system protection measures at co-located facilities to ensure they operate within their requested injection and withdrawal rights.
quotes: Vistra supports enabling transmission providers to identify and impose requirements to ensure that co-located facilities inject and withdraw according to their rights, as well as other measures necessary to ensure reliable operation of the transmission system.

letters.desc: Bloom supports requiring system protection equipment but urges FERC to define unauthorized injections narrowly. Penalties should apply only to intentional, sustained non-compliance, not to unavoidable transient flows. Technical minimums should align with IEEE 1547-2018 and NERC IBR guidelines.
quotes: The scope of the term "unauthorized" must be addressed.  Bloom urges the Commission to distinguish between inadvertent or transient injections (authorized injections), and sustained or intentional injections that result in malfunction or non-compliance with transmission provider or RTO directives (unauthorized injections).

Any minimum technical requirements should be consistent with existing standards, such as IEEE 1547-2018 and emerging NERC IBR performance and modeling guidelines to avoid duplicative or conflicting requirements.

letters.desc: While not opposing system protection facility requirements for hybrid facilities, the filer cautions that such equipment does not guarantee prevention of unauthorized injections or withdrawals, making separate metering essential for reliability.
quotes: system protection facilities do not guarantee the prevention of unauthorized injections or withdrawals.  This is one of the reasons that it is imperative from a reliability perspective that the load and generation of a hybrid facility are studied and metered separately.

letters.desc: Buckeye opposes relying on individual utility-to-data-center agreements as a substitute for a consistent federal framework, arguing such agreements are insufficiently protective of third-party wholesale customers and create inconsistent treatment across the system.
quotes: The Commission cannot assume that agreements negotiated between one utility and a data center will be sufficiently protective of other customers.

letters.desc: Based on California's experience, the proposed three-year forward look in reliability studies for co-located generation is too short to capture load growth and system condition impacts relevant to reliability.
quotes: in California's experience, studies looking out only three years would likely be insufficient to fully assess system conditions, load growth, and potential reliability impacts.

letters.desc: Consumers Energy warns that large load customers lack the industry expertise generators have accumulated over decades, making an option to build interconnection facilities a reliability hazard. The Commission lacks sufficient record to support extending that option.
quotes: the Company is concerned that allowing large load customers the option to build may carry unintended reliability risks given that many large load customers are data centers or other large industrial customers that lack the industry expertise required to ensure safe and reliable grid operations.

letters.desc: Studying only net contractual rights for hybrid facilities ignores independent load and generation behavior during planned or forced outages. Duke Energy argues full withdrawal and injection capabilities must be evaluated to protect grid reliability.
quotes: Transmission providers must have the ability to study all load and generation, including hybrid facilities, in a manner that reflects the potential actual operating impacts to the grid.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy contends that system protection facilities cannot substitute for proper interconnection studies because they fail roughly 6% of the time and are overridden by contingencies. NERC standard PRC-012-2 requires planners to account for exactly these failures.
quotes: customer-specific information is often confidential under state law or contract, in which case FirstEnergy is required to maintain such information as strictly confidential unless the customer otherwise consents to its disclosure.
netting fails to provide the redundant protection necessary for the system to perform reliably.
Protective equipment that would enforce a net amount is not a failsafe; to the contrary, such equipment suffers from an approximately 6% failure rate.
contingencies and control failures routinely defeat netting.

Transmission owners can ensure compliance much more efficiently when they are the ones building facilities in the first place.  It is not just or reasonable to make transmission owners responsible for reliability of network upgrades constructed by others.

letters.org: Louisiana Public Service CommissionMississippi Public Service Commission
letters.desc: States have both the authority and the duty to ensure that the costs of serving large loads do not fall unfairly on retail ratepayers. Federal preemption of load interconnection removes that protective layer.
quotes: the states have the authority and duty to develop protective measures in approving facilities needed to serve large loads, including measures designed to fairly allocate the costs and to protect reliability so that retail ratepayers are not unfairly burdened

letters.desc: The PA PUC warns that FERC-mandated interconnections without sufficient generation capacity could threaten reliability for existing retail customers during peak demand or extreme weather. It also argues the ANOPR could preempt state protective tools such as large load tariffs and flexibility requirements.
quotes: The ANOPR proposes an unprecedented expansion of Federal jurisdiction and potential intrusion on the states' historic retail regulatory authority under the Federal Power Act, introducing potential confusion, unintended customer consequences, and/or legal uncertainty where none currently exists.

FERC-mandated large load interconnections without sufficient available generation capacity could threaten reliable power service to existing retail customers, as grid operators may lack the resources needed to maintain system stability during peak demand or extreme weather events.
The proposals in the ANOPR could limit a state's ability to implement protective measures, such as large load tariffs and flexibility requirements.

The recommendations that (1) load and hybrid facilities be studied together with generating facilities for efficient siting and be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties; (2) hybrid facilities be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested to provide incentives for co-location with new generation facilities; (3) any hybrid interconnection install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights; (4) financial penalties for load facilities and hybrid facilities; (5) expedited consideration of interconnection studies of large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable; and (6) that load and hybrid facilities should be responsible for 100% of the network upgrades that are assigned through the interconnection studies all have widespread economic and political ramifications.

letters.desc: PJM opposes reducing reliability planning standards under a "connect-and-manage" approach without thorough cost-benefit analysis, arguing that treating curtailable load as non-firm in long-term planning could degrade grid reliability for the entire region.
quotes: the proposed reforms appear to signal an openness to a less-reliable planning paradigm for new generation facilities (see, e.g., Principles 3 and 5) where hybrid facilities involving "new generation facilities" are studied based solely on injection and/or withdrawal rights requested, and large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable will have their studies expedited so that such facilities can be put into operation with greater speed.
Has this tradeoff between reliability and speed to market been sufficiently vetted, and are the potential costs documented and understood?

The "connect-and-manage" framework could lead to future grid build out that is not as robust and reliable as the planning standard PJM (and other RTOs/ISOs) have adhered to for decades if voluntarily curtailable load (Principle 7) is not planned for as firm load in regional transmission planning processes.

The NERC Large Load Task Force is well-equipped to continue its work in exploring cutting-edge issues relating to the planning for and operational complexities of a grid with growing large load saturation.  That industry wide forum drawing together deep subject matter expertise is the best forum to develop new standards and issue other necessary guidance to inform reliable system operations and planning involving large loads.

letters.org: PSEG CompaniesPSEG Energy Resources & Trade LLCPSEG Power LLC ,Public Service Electric and Gas Company ,
letters.desc: PSEG opposes applying SSR/RMR-type studies to co-located load arrangements. It contends such studies are designed for generator retirement decisions, not co-location, and applying them here would be unduly discriminatory under the FPA.
quotes: applying such a study to co-located load arrangement would be unduly discriminatory under the FPA because it would treat co-located load arrangements differently than loads seeking to interconnect on a front of the meter basis.
layering on an RMR study that examines resource adequacy issues is unnecessary, inefficient, unduly discriminatory, and not the correct legal or practical fit for these arrangements.

letters.desc: SMA argues that penalties for unauthorized injections or withdrawals are unnecessary when system protection settings are well coordinated at the overall system level, and that disconnection is itself harmful to the customer.
quotes: SMA's perspective is that penalties are not necessary if system protection settings are well coordinated and operate effectively at the overall system level.

letters.desc: The Senator asks whether tech company public commitments to fund their own infrastructure costs are credible and enforceable. The question implies skepticism but stops short of a policy recommendation.
quotes: Prominent technology companies have made public commitments to "pay their own way" when it comes to data center power usage and infrastructure costs. Does FERC assess these to be credible and/or enforceable commitments?
